author: Johana Bhuiyan
description:
California judge finds company ‘vicariously liable’ for driver’s negligence in death of Emily Normandin-Parker

Uber was ordered to pay $40m to the parents of a 23-year-old woman who was killed after a driver kicked her and a friend out of his car by the side of a California freeway, according to newly public arbitration documents.

An arbitrator, retired Calfornia judge Richard A Stone, found that the ride-share company was “vicariously liable” for the driver’s negligence.

Continue reading...
title: Uber ordered to pay $40m over death of woman ejected by driver on freeway

author: Lucy Campbell
description:
Angela Lipps, 50, has alleged in suit that Fargo police wrongly relied on AI facial recognition to charge and arrest

A Tennessee woman who was falsely charged with bank theft in North Dakota and jailed for six months has sued for $10m in damages, alleging in a federal lawsuit that Fargo police improperly relied on an artificial intelligence (AI) facial recognition system to wrongly accuse her.

Angela Lipps, 50, was arrested at gunpoint by US marshals at her home in Tennessee while babysitting her neighbor’s four children in July 2025. The mother of three and grandmother of five was booked into a county jail and remained there for almost four months without bail while awaiting extradition to North Dakota, where she was held for about two more months.

Continue reading..
title: Tennessee woman falsely charged with bank theft in North Dakota sues for $10m in damages

author: Roque Planas
description:
Customs and Border Protection faces bipartisan backlash from locals for 30ft border wall through Texas national park

The Trump administration is pressing forward with construction on the controversial border wall in the Big Bend region of west Texas, even as Customs and Border Protection (CBP) faces furious backlash from local leaders and landowners for its fast-moving plans.

Construction began this week in Hudspeth county, which lies just east of th
title: Trump administration pushes on with construction of controversial Big Bend border wall

author: Uwa Ede-Osifo
description:
Suspect charged with attempted murder as driver, identified by surname Singh, reportedly stabbed 17 times

A Sikh truck driver survived harrowing attack in which he was beaten then stabbed 17 times in a rest stop off a Wyoming highway on Sunday, according to news reports.

The suspected assailant, Andrew Kris Bzdak, reportedly fled the scene, before Wyoming highway patrol troopers arrested him, the Sacramento Bee reported.

Continue reading...
title: Sikh truck driver survives harrowing stabbing attack at Wyoming rest stop

author: Robert Tait in Washington
description:
Lindsey O Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act signed into law two days after House passed it in bipartisan vote

Donald Trump on Friday signed legislation enabling sweeping sanctions on Russia aimed at pressing it into ending its war with Ukraine, and also giving him the power to impose additional tariffs on countries breaking the embargo.

The US president signed the Lindsey O Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act into law two days after it passed the House of Representatives in a bipartisan 262-159 vote, amid concerns the legislation gives him too much power.

Continue reading...
title: Trump signs bill imposing sanctions on Russia and giving him more power to levy tariffs

author: Marina Dunbar
description:
Madison Rebecca Colello, 29, surrenders after 20 other cats in severe distress rescued from business in town of Walker

A Louisiana woman faces dozens of animal cruelty charges after 17 cats were found dead at a local business amid dangerously hot conditions without food or water, with 20 other cats in severe distress being rescued.

Madison Rebecca Colello, 29, surrendered on Thursday morning at the Livingston parish detention center in Walker, Louisiana. She faces 17 felony counts of aggravated animal cruelty – in connection with the dead cats – and 37 misdemeanor counts of animal cruelty.

Continue reading...
title: Louisiana woman faces charges after 17 cats found dead in extreme-heat conditions

author: Dani Anguiano
description:
Navy veteran David Voight, his wife, Amy, and their child were found dead as relatives report Voight was suffering from PTSD

Authorities are investigating what led to the tragic case of a family who was found fatally shot in their San Diego area home on Wednesday morning.

The San Diego police department identified the family as Amy Voight, 54, and David Voight, 56, and the couple’s 13-year-old daughter. The family died of gunshot wounds, police said, and investigators found a weapon in the residence.

Continue reading...
title: San Diego police investigate case of family of three found fatally shot in home

author: Jess Cartner-Morley
description:
Debut runway show with affordable pieces reflects resurgent style confidence at retailer after hit releases

Joan Collins declared the coats “very chic”, and has her eye on a graceful ivory evening dress with caped shoulders. Kemi Badenoch plans to snap up the classic black tuxedo jacket. If the British public are as enthusiastic as the celebrity front row, Marks & Spencer’s first ever London fashion week catwalk looks like a hit.

The show, held at the Design Museum for 310 guests including Ian Wright and Jamie Carragher, was a gamble on both sides. Would snobby fashionistas be traumatised by elasticated waistbands and practical rainwear? Would M&S customers be alienated by a world of £2,000 handbags and shoes you can’t walk in?

Continue reading...
title: M&S marks 100 years of selling fashion with LFW catwalk show

author: Presented by Lucy Hough with Aaron Sharp; produced by Angus Nealeand Bryony Moore; senior producer Ryan Ramgobin; executive producer Zoe Hitch
description:
Buckingham Palace has issued a rare, and strong, rebuttal to claims made in Earl Spencer’s memoir Swan Song. The book claims that King Charles told Spencer days after Diana’s death and during a heated row over funeral arrangements: ‘Rest assured, we’ll forget her soon enough.’ Lucy Hough speaks to the Guardian’s senior national news editor, Aaron Sharp

Continue reading...
title: Diana book sparks royal row between King Charles and Earl Spencer - The Latest

author: Benita Kolovos Victorian state correspondent
description:
Party has unveiled a steady stream of contenders for state election, including a former councillor who lost his licence for drink-driving

  • Get our new political email, free app or daily news podcast

Candidates contesting the Victorian state election for One Nation include a former Liberal who has won support from alleged underworld figures, a naturopath who has endorsed Donald Trump’s unfounded claim that paracetamol is linked to autism and a former shire councillor who lost his licence for drink-driving.

Pauline Hanson announced who would be her party’s upper house candidates and
title: Alleged underworld supporters and unfounded health claims: One Nation rolls out more Victorian election candidates

author: Rob Davies
description:
There are ‘insufficient funds’ to pay unpaid wages, tax owed to HMRC and overdue bills, accountants say

Accountants picking over the remains of BrewDog, the “punk” beer company that collapsed earlier this year, have said that creditors who are owed about £190m will not be paid back.

In an update on their progress, administrators at AlixPartners warned there were “insufficient funds” to pay debts in full related to unpaid wages, tax owed to HM Revenue and Customs, and overdue bills from other businesses.

Continue reading...
title: BrewDog creditors owed £190m will not be paid in full, say administrators

author: Tom Perkins
description:
Soil and water around military bases show elevated levels of Pfas pollution due to chemicals used in firefighting foam

Many US military veterans have much higher levels of Pfas “forever chemicals” in their blood than non-veterans, new peer-reviewed research finds, raising more questions about health risks the nation’s service members face after serving at polluted bases.

Ground water, surface water and soil around military bases show among the highest levels of Pfas pollution in the US because the chemicals are used in firefighting foam deployed during training and emergencies. While the problem has been clear for over a decade, the new Brown University-led study is the first to compare levels in veterans’ blood with those in civilians.
title: US veterans have greater levels of Pfas in their blood than civilians, new study finds

author: Gwyn Topham Transport correspondent
description:
UK ministers say report into incident leaves questions unanswered over why problem was not discovered and fixed earlier

  • Business live – latest updates

A software defect in part of the UK’s air traffic control system corrupted flight data “in the space of a millisecond”, leading to a six-hour outage and mass airline cancellations and delays across the UK last week, National Air Traffic Services has said.

But ministers said that the report into the incident still left questions unanswered, saying they needed “to urgently understand why this issue was not discovered and fixed before it caused chaos”.
title: Flight chaos for hundreds of thousands was caused in ‘millisecond’ by software error

author: Patrick Wintour Diplomatic editor
description:
Jagtar Singh Johal, from Scotland, was arrested after wedding in Punjab on alleged terrorism offences

Jagtar Singh Johal, a British Sikh man who was arrested in India in 2017 in connection with alleged terrorism offences, has been granted bail by a Delhi court.

Johal, from Scotland, was arrested for his alleged role in funding the Khalistan Liberation Force, which had carried out targeted killings in India’s Punjab region.

Continue reading...
title: British Sikh man granted bail in India nine years after arrest

author: George Zornick
description:
The extraordinary danger is that a president who believes he is the law, and the law is him, remains intent on disrupting the electoral process

  • This was originally published in The Stakes 2026, a newsletter about the midterm elections. Sign up to get it in your inbox

For the millions of Americans who vote by mail – almost a third of the country – the week began with significant uncertainty that they would be able to easily submit their ballot this fall, thanks to a March executive order from Donald Trump that aimed to restrict mail-in ballots. By Monday night, the supreme court restored a measure of order by rebuking the president and
title: What Trump’s attacks on mail-in voting mean for the midterms

author: Jessica Glenza in Pittsburgh, Pennsylania
description:
Participants in Pittsburgh may never learn the results of their cognitive tests – and funding cuts that target ‘DEI’ have the potential to delay vital diagnoses

Roderick Blair was surprised when scientific researchers appeared on his doorstep in the Homewood neighborhood of Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania.

Here, on a recent summer day, police cars, an ambulance and a TV reporter crowded into a driveway on the edge of the neighborhood. A helicopter swung overhead. Saplings peeked over rooflines from gutters, windows were broken, screens tattered, doors boarded up and rippling sidewalks crumbled. Bedraggled chain link fences held back the season’s tall grass.

Continue reading...
title: ‘Clear retribution’: dismay as key Alzheimer’s study cancelled amid Trump attacks on science

author: Frances Ryan and Patrick Butler
description:
Campaigners describe ‘brazenly discriminatory’ practices around funding from NHS care boards

  • UK politics live – latest updates

Disabled people must have a guaranteed right to travel abroad, MPs and peers have said, as further cases emerged of individuals barred from taking holidays as a result of “ridiculous” rules imposed by local NHS care boards and local councils.

Leading figures have called on the government to bring in clear national guidelines to ensure people who require full-time personal assistants (PAs) are not prevented from using funding for their 24/7 support team for breaks and work trips.
title: Disabled people in UK need right to travel abroad, say MPs, after ‘ridiculous’ restrictions

author: Debbie Carlson
description:
Some experts worry factors affecting wheat exports could push global food prices even higher than they are now

Wheat prices are at their highest level in three years, which means farmer Merrill Nielsen should be getting more for his crops out of his 2,500-acre (1,010-hectare) Kansas farm.

Yet even as future prices for bread-type wheat are up 39%, Nielsen is unsure whether increased prices will raise his bottom line. The price of diesel fuel, which he needs to run his tractor, has hit record highs. Then there’s the erratic weather that made him lose his entire wheat crop in the spring, and drought has overtaken the southern Great Plains.

Continue reading...
title: US wheat farmers navigate uncertainty amid drought and geopolitical chaos

author: Michael Sainato
description:
Company may have spent about $200,000 to fight union effort in White Plains, where 11 people can vote to join UAW

Workers at an AutoZone in White Plains, New York, are seeking to become the first store at the US’s largest auto parts retailer to win a union election, set to begin 25 September, despite a heavy-handed union opposition campaign from the company.

LaborLab, a non-profit workers’-rights watchdog, estimates AutoZone has spent around $200,000 to oppose the unionization effort at the White Plains store, where 11 workers are eligible to vote to join the United Auto Workers Local 259. The estimate is based on external attorney costs and internal costs of executive salaries based on reports from workers at the store.
title: Workers in New York seek to create first AutoZone union as company resists

author: Gwyn Topham Transport correspondent
description:
Hundreds of cars driven through cones or barriers in England this year, says National Highways

Drivers ignoring roadwork closures to skip queues are putting lives at risk, National Highways has warned, after recording hundreds of incidents this year where cars were deliberately driven through cones or barriers.

The agency, which manages motorways and major roads, said there was increasing concern about incursions into closed-off roadworks and the danger they posed.

Continue reading...
title: Drivers ignoring roadwork closures to skip queues ‘wilfully putting lives at risk’

author: Nicola Slawson
description:
When Mohammad Abdul Zinati, 15, rushed to help a man wounded in a bomb attack, he had no time to react before he too was hit. Plus, meet the cartographers who took on centuries of western bias

Good morning.

Mohammad Abdul Zinati was walking home from school through the rubble of Salah Khalaf Street in northern Gaza City when he stopped at a supermarket where a group of classmates and friends had gathered.

What has Israel said about the incident? The Israeli military said the incident was under review. The IDF has repeatedly rejected allegations that it deliberately targets civilians, saying it assesses and takes into account the risk of civilian harm when carrying out strikes.

What has Trump said about South Korea? Trump has criticised Seoul for what he called insufficient support for the Iran war ‌and scaled back major joint military drills by the two countries’ armed forces this summer, a move that unsettled the US ally.</
title: First Thing: Witnesses recount Israeli ‘double-tap’ strike that killed child and medic in Gaza

author: Ramon Antonio Vargas
description:
The African serval, illegally enclosed in the back yard, was subdued and transferred to an animal welfare facility

Louisiana firefighters responding to a small house blaze found a wildcat native to sub-Saharan Africa illegally enclosed in the back yard, and an animal welfare agency is now seeking to place the creature in an appropriate environment, according to officials.

Firefighters investigating a report of a minor fire at a home in the suburban New Orleans community of Marrero on Tuesday spotted the cat in question – an African serval – behind the residence in a chain-linked enclosure resembling a cramped baseball batting cage, a spokesperson for the local animal protection services said.

Continue reading...
title: Louisiana firefighters find feline native to sub-Saharan Africa while responding to house fire

author: Luca Ittimani
description:
Liberal MP speaks of AI’s shortcomings as cyber chief tells inquiry the tech is needed to fend off ‘highly capable malicious cyber actors’

  • Get our new political email, free app or daily news podcast

When a man with a terminal illness wrote to his local MP Andrew Hastie, telling him he planned on ending his own life with voluntary assisted dying, Microsoft Copilot suggested Hastie reply with “congratulations!”, “great to hear from you” or “that is wonderful news!”.

Hastie shared the episode at a parliamentary inquiry on Friday to underline the shortcomings of the American-run software as he called for AI run by Australians.
title: Andrew Hastie says AI advised him to reply ‘congratulations!’ to man who planned to end life with assisted dying

author: Andrew Sparrow
description:
It will be the first time the PM uses No 10 North to host an overseas visit while the chancellor will be in Dublin meeting with EU finance ministers

Here is the statement Tom Watson issued about his decision to take a job with Palantir.

I’m terrifically excited to be joining the young Palantir team who make the tools that public service workers need to transform how they serve the British people.

Whether that means reducing the time it takes to be diagnosed, treated and discharged from hospital, helping our military personnel keep us safe and secure, or enabling our police to crack crimes and root out corruption, Palantir software can transform the country’s public services.

Continue reading...
title: Burnham to meet Irish PM as UK bids to get exemptions from EU’s ‘Made in Europe’ plan – UK politics live

author: James Michelin for MetDesk
description:
At least one person dead as stormy weather causes severe flooding in Barcelona and Valencia

Intense and slow-moving thunderstorms broke out on Wednesday afternoon across parts of eastern Spain, bringing some severe flooding and killing at least one person.

Storms first struck over the Castilla-La Mancha regionduring the afternoon before passing over Spain’s east coast, becoming very slow-moving and continuing overnight. Torrential rainfall, strong winds and large hail were reported in Valencia and Barcelona, causing widespread flooding in both cities. Weather stations west of Barcelona recorded some of the highest totals with more than 100mm (4in) of rain falling in the space of a few hours, and locally 70mm in just 30 minutes in the early hours of Thursday morning. Cars and roads were submerged, and flights were cancelled across the region.
title: Weather tracker: Thunderstorms hit Spain as Japan braces for typhoon

author: Caitlin Cassidy and Sarah Basford Canales
description:
Australian Greens senator compares government’s policy to ICE as Tony Burke calls it a ‘ridiculous claim’

  • Get our new political email, free app or daily news podcast

The federal government’s move to reopen detention centres for visa overstayers, overseen by compliance officers, has drawn comparison from the Greens and advocates to Donald Trump’s sweeping immigration crackdown in the United States.

The home affairs minister, Tony Burke, was careful to downplay any similarities when he announced the federal government’s immigrati
title: Labor visa overstayer detention centre plan branded a ‘Donald Trump twist’ on immigration

author: Jamie Grierson
description:
Patients among hundreds who suffered harm at County Durham and Darlington foundation trust’s breast unit

Twenty women had their breasts removed unnecessarily while being treated for cancer at an NHS trust in north-east England.

The County Durham and Darlington foundation trust (CDDFT) told the BBC that the women were among hundreds of patients who came to harm during treatment at its breast unit.

Continue reading...
title: Twenty women had breasts removed unnecessarily during NHS cancer care

author: Catie McLeod
description:
Warwick Levy, who runs Lonely Kids Club, says AI may have been used to scrape his entire website and replicate designs

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

After 15 years running a small business making T-shirts, Warwick Levy says it was “brutal” when he first discovered an identical design for sale on Temu.

It turned out there was an overwhelming amount of T-shirts identical to his own for sale on the Chinese e-commerce marketplace. Between 2025 and earlier this year, Levy, 37, found thousands of rip-offs.

Continue reading...
title: ‘Brutal’: thousands of T-shirt designs stolen and listed on Temu, Sydney label claims

author: Achol Arok
description:
Authorities called to Sorrento Beach on Friday morning following reports of shark-related incident

A man has died after being bitten by a shark off Sorrento Beach in Perth’s north.

Emergency services were called to the popular Sorrento Beach about 10.30am on Friday after reports of a shark-related incident.

Continue reading...
title: Swimmer dies after being bitten by shark off popular Perth beach

author: Nino Bucci
description:
Detective senior constable is due to face court in Ballarat next month on common assault charge

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

A Victorian detective allegedly punched and kicked a teenager multiple times while they were handcuffed and compliant during an arrest last year, the state’s corruption watchdog says.

The independent broad-based anti-corruption commission (Ibac) said on Friday that it had charged the detective senior constable with common assault in relation to the October 2025 incident in Ballarat.

Continue reading...
title: Victorian police officer charged after allegedly punching and kicking handcuffed teenager during arrest

author: Robert Booth UK technology editor
description:
Peer takes full-time position at the controversial company as it fends off pressure from both Andy Burnham’s government and Sadiq Khan

Another former government minister has been hired by a controversial US AI company, this time Palantir, which has appointed Andy Burnham’s former ministerial colleague Tom Watson.

The Labour peer and former deputy leader will operate alongside Palantir’s UK and Europe chief executive, Louis Mosley, as the company attempts to fend off pressure on Burnham’s government to axe its £330m NHS contract. It is also fighting Sadiq Khan in court over the Labour London mayor’s block on a £50m contract to use its AI in Metropolitan police investigations. Palantir also wants to win more public sector work in the UK, where it
title: Former Labour deputy leader Tom Watson joins Palantir

author: Penry Buckley
description:
Sharangan Maheswaran denies message he received about NSW minister was related to work for fugitive property developer

  • Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

  • Get our new political email, free app or daily news podcast

A former Labor councillor says he had a “common interest” with a conservative Liberal operative, but denied that a message he received about damaging the reputation of NSW Liberal minister David Elliot was related to political work for a fugitive property developer, an inquiry has heard.

Sharangan Maheswaran told the Independent Commission Against Corrupti

description:
Former prime minister says US would ‘scuttle itself back to San Diego’, leaving Australia to deal with retribution from China

Aukus critic Paul Keating has said the submarine deal is locking Australia in to any future US conflict with China – “a war America would certainly lose” – and making Australia a target for retribution.

title: Paul Keating says Aukus locking Australia into a US war against China, which it would ‘certainly lose’

description:
Tech bosses have called for a slowdown in artificial intelligence and the creation of formal guardrails from the US government. author: Australian Associated Press
description:
‘Disposal of the body in this case was as thorough as it was brutal,’ justice Peter Hamill said when sentencing 55-year-old Nirmeen Noufl

  • Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

A woman who lied to police multiple times to cover up killing and dismembering her abusive husband will spend a further 12 months in jail.

Nirmeen Noufl was sentenced on Friday to at least three years in jail after pleading guilty in August to killing her husband, Mamdouh Noufl, in excessive self-defence while she was being choked
title: Sydney woman sentenced for killing and dismembering abusive husband

author: Uwa Ede-Osifo
description:
Bailee Lynn Rios, 36, accused of driving on wrong side of road to cause fatal crash NBC news helicopter was covering

A California woman was allegedly driving under the influence when she sped down the wrong side of the road, ran a red light and plowed her SUV into a Los Angeles metro bus on Tuesday, killing two passengers, prosecutors say, in a tragedy compounded when a news helicopter covering the crash plummeted from the sky, killing three.

Bailee Lynn Rios, 36, has been charged with two counts of murder over the deaths of the two people on the bus, identified as Daniel Castillo, 46, and Gage Weida, 31. Rios was being held on $4.1m bail and is set to be arraigned on 18 September. Online court records did not list a lawyer who might speak on her behalf, and the public defender’s office did not immediately return a message about whether it was representing her.

C
title: LA woman charged with murder over bus crash that preceded deadly helicopter plunge
